page: Google Cloud Platform n1-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance based on the x86_64 architecture. It features 4 vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, providing 2 threads per core. The instance is equipped with an Intel Xeon CPU operating at a base frequency of 2.3 GHz, featuring a 45 MB L3 cache, 0.25 MB L2 cache, and 32 KB L1d cache. It includes 15.0 GB of dedicated system memory, yielding 3.75 GB of RAM per vCPU. This instance does not bundle local storage or GPU accelerators, and it includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations place the n1-standard-4 in the lower performance tiers. In CPU-intensive tests, the instance achieved a stress-ng single-core score of 1107.78 and a multi-core score of 2904.55, both falling into the bottom 25 percent of tested hardware. Memory bandwidth tests showed 161.64 GB/sec for cached small blocks, dropping to 25.29 GB/sec for uncached large block reads and 21.61 GB/sec for writes. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression speeds were registered at 19.01 GB/sec and 7.14 GB/sec respectively, indicating limited throughput for data serialization tasks.

Given its hardware profile, the n1-standard-4 represents an entry-level general-purpose tier. It is designed for workloads with modest computational demands, such as basic web serving, light database operations, or small-scale software compilation. The instance's qualitative cost efficiency lies in its balanced resource allocation for non-critical development and testing environments, though its lower benchmark scores suggest it is less optimal for high-throughput production systems or intensive data processing.
